proof.text: Write $P_V$ for restriction along $B_V\to A_V$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. This coefficient map is induced by $\bar r\mapsto r1_A$: it is well defined because $n1_A=0$, and central because integer multiples of $1_A$ commute with every element. Apply [lem-exc-proetale-finite-scalar-unit-comparison] to $B\to A$ and to $i,j$. Thus scalar restriction commutes with these inverse and direct images and takes the actual $A$-unit, through the displayed comparisons, to the $B$-unit. Scalar restriction detects zero objects and reflects isomorphisms: it leaves all underlying abelian sheaves and maps unchanged. Explicitly, the inverse of an invertible underlying map $v$ of $A$-module sheaves is $A$-linear, since applying $v$ to $v^{-1}(ax)$ and $av^{-1}(x)$ gives $ax$ in both cases.

proof.text: If $j_A^*N=0$, the inverse-image comparison gives $j_B^*P_TN=0$. The assumed [lem-exc-proetale-closed-essential-image], applied with the commutative ring sheaves $B_V$, says exactly that $\eta^B_{i,P_TN}$ is invertible. By the unit equation in [lem-exc-proetale-finite-scalar-unit-comparison], $P_T(\eta^A_{i,N})$ is invertible; Step 1 reflects this to an $A_T$-linear isomorphism. Naturality is the naturality of the closed adjunction unit itself. For an $A_Z$-module sheaf $M$, the direct-image comparison identifies $P_Ti_{A,*}M$ with $i_{B,*}P_ZM$. This object is in the essential image of $i_{B,*}$, so the other implication of [lem-exc-proetale-closed-essential-image] gives $j_B^*P_Ti_{A,*}M=0$. Comparing inverse images and detecting zero gives $j_A^*i_{A,*}M=0$. The quasi-compact open-complement hypothesis needed for the assumed lemma is precisely the hypothesis on $j$.

proof.text: For any $A_T$-module sheaf $N$, put $G(N)=\ker(\eta^A_{j,N})$. First, $j_B^*(\eta^B_{j,P_TN})$ is invertible: by [lem-pur-proetale-open-unit-evaluation], after restricting to an object $W\to U$ it is the restriction map from $W$ to $W\times_TU\cong W$, hence the identity. The comparison and unit equation of [lem-exc-proetale-finite-scalar-unit-comparison], and Step 1, therefore show that $j_A^*(\eta^A_{j,N})$ is invertible. Exactness of $j_A^*$ in [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact] gives $j_A^*G(N)\cong\ker(j_A^*\eta^A_{j,N})=0$. Step 2, now applied to $G(N)$, identifies its actual closed unit $G(N)\xrightarrow{\sim}i_*i^*G(N)=i_*H(N)$.

source.place: Supported kernel identification and assembly of the degreewise short exact sequences

proof.text: Let $k_q:F^q\to I^q$ be the kernel inclusion and write $\eta_q=\eta_{j,I^q}$. Naturality gives $\eta_{q+1}d_I^q=(j_*j^*d_I^q)\eta_q$, so $d_I^q k_q$ is killed by $\eta_{q+1}$. The sectionwise kernel description in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] defines a unique restriction $d_F^q:F^q\to F^{q+1}$ with $k_{q+1}d_F^q=d_I^qk_q$. Since $k_{q+2}d_F^{q+1}d_F^q=d_I^{q+1}d_I^qk_q=0$ and $k_{q+2}$ is monic, $d_F^{q+1}d_F^q=0$. Define $H(I)^q=i^*F^q$ and $d_{H(I)}^q=i^*(d_F^q)$. The closed units $u_q:F^q\to i_*i^*F^q$, invertible by Step 3, satisfy $u_{q+1}d_F^q=(i_*i^*d_F^q)u_q$ by naturality. Thus $u:F\to i_*H(I)$ is a chain map, and $d_F^qu_q^{-1}=u_{q+1}^{-1}(i_*i^*d_F^q)$ shows that the degreewise inverses form its inverse chain map.

source.place: Supported kernel identification and assembly of the degreewise short exact sequences

proof.text: By hypothesis each $\eta_q$ is epic. In the abelian module-sheaf category of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], $k_q$ is its kernel, hence $0\to F^q\xrightarrow{k_q}I^q\xrightarrow{\eta_q}j_*j^*I^q\to0$ is short exact. Replacing $F^q$ by $i_*H(I)^q$ through $u_q$, the first arrow is exactly $k_qu_q^{-1}$. Step 4 makes these arrows chain maps, and [lem-weil-pbc-cochain-complexes-degreewise-exact] gives the asserted short exact sequence of complexes. For any chain map $a:I\to I'$, naturality of $\eta_j$ restricts each $a^q$ to $F^q\to F'^q$, and naturality of $\eta_i$ makes its square with $u_q,u'_q$ commute. The kernel inclusions also commute with $a^q$ by construction, so the whole short exact sequence is natural in $I$.

title: Finite-ring supported units and kernel complexes
statement:
Let $T$ be a Noetherian scheme (locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]), let $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] with quasi-compact complementary open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow T$ [def-weil-open-immersion], and let $A$ be a finite ring, not necessarily commutative. Use the coefficient sheaves $A_S$ and left module categories on the small pro-etale sites of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], with inverse images and units from [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image, prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map, prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact]. Put $n=\operatorname{ord}_{(A,+)}(1_A)\geq1$ and $B=\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z$, with its central map $B\to A$. Assume that, for the commutative coefficient sheaves $B_S$, the essential image of $i_*$ is precisely the sheaves killed by $j^*$ and their closed adjunction units are isomorphisms, as stated in [lem-exc-proetale-closed-essential-image].

Then for every left $A_T$-module sheaf $N$ with $j^*N=0$, the actual $A_T$-linear closed unit $N\to i_*i^*N$ is an isomorphism, naturally in $N$. For every left $A_Z$-module sheaf $M$, one has $j^*i_*M=0$.

For any cochain complex $I$ of left $A_T$-module sheaves such that every termwise open unit $I^q\to j_*j^*I^q$ is epic, let $F^q=\ker(I^q\to j_*j^*I^q)$ in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and put $H(N)=i^*\ker(N\to j_*j^*N)$. The differentials of $I$ restrict to these kernels, and the closed units form an isomorphism of complexes $F\xrightarrow{\sim}i_*H(I)$. Composing its inverse with the kernel inclusion gives a natural short exact sequence of complexes
$$0\longrightarrow i_*H(I)\longrightarrow I\longrightarrow j_*j^*I\longrightarrow0,$$
where short exact means short exact in each degree [lem-weil-pbc-cochain-complexes-degreewise-exact].

Step 2's transfer is therefore exact, and in any case invertibility of a unit does not depend on the choice of isomorphic left adjoint. Step 1: Z/n to A is well defined and central, and scalar restriction reflects isomorphisms and detects zero. Step 2: the unit equation gives P(eta^A_i) = iso composed with eta^B_i, and beta and alpha give j^*i_*M=0. The quasi-compact j hypothesis matches. Step 3: j^*eta_j is the identity by the restriction description of open-unit-evaluation (finite commutative B), kernel preservation gives j^*G=0, and Step 2 applies to G. Steps 4-5: the kernel differential, d^2=0, the chain map u and its inverse, the degreewise short exact sequence with epic eta, and naturality are all correct. The helper is true: both ring-map composites agree on constant sections, the underlying maps are identities, and the module units have the abelian unit as underlying map.
